cs.t: I own a big variety of methods because I think it's fun, but get the most use out of our Toddy [1]. You can make 15-20 cups of cold brew at once (which has a decent shelf life) and if you use the optional filter bags, cleanup is super easy. With nice beans you can also make some really flavorful coffee, but it's extremely tolerant of cheap/old beans in a pinch. For hot coffee the aeropress has the best convenience to consistent quality ratio, but v60 pourover cone gives you the most control over all the variables, for better or for worse. If you're new to coffee, don't sweat the method and focus on getting decent beans that are less than a week old. A good filter for roaster quality is if they have a 'roasted on' date, vs no date or a 'best by' date. [1] -  https://toddycafe.com/
